reference: GNU patch 2.8 (and GNU diffutils diff for the round trip; GNU ed 1.21.1 for -e, which GNU patch runs), compared for stdout, status and the resulting files, including .orig and .rej.
coverage: Guest pass 3 G45: fuzz is capped at the hunk's context, so deleted lines must match; zero- and one-line-context hunks fail rather than overwrite.
Ordinary fuzz on a context line, and diff -ruN | patch -p1 creating and removing files.

Guest pass 4 G55: context diffs (diff -c, -C N): one and several hunks, omitted sides, -R, -p with diff -rcN creating and removing files, missing newlines, offsets, reversed-patch detection and GNU's context-form rejects (also for normal diffs).

Guest pass 5 G80: -e/--ed applies a diff -e script as GNU patch does through ed: hunks of a/c/d/i/s commands, skipped garbage, ed FAILED, -o (appending each hunk's result), -b, --dry-run and an unfinished last line.
exclusions: Interactive questions on a terminal are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: G45: a zero-context hunk whose '-' line does not match fails (no fuzz is possible without context): Hunk FAILED, f.rej and f.orig written, file unchanged, status 1.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
DIFFERENT
four
five
' > f
printf -- '--- f
+++ f
@@ -3 +3 @@
-three
+THREE
' > p0
patch f < p0 || echo rc=$?
cat f f.rej

cases.purpose: G45: a one-line hunk -a +b on a file holding z fails instead of overwriting it.
cases.script:
echo z > s
printf -- '--- s
+++ s
@@ -1 +1 @@
-a
+b
' > p1
patch s < p1 || echo rc=$?
cat s

cases.purpose: G45/G46: a diff -ruN patch applied with patch -p1 recreates the new tree: changed, created and deleted (Epoch-dated, now empty) files; the deleted file is removed.
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC
mkdir -p a/sub b/sub b/onlyb
printf '1\n2\n' > a/x
printf '1\nTWO\n' > b/x
echo o > a/sub/old
echo k > a/sub/keep
echo K > b/sub/keep
echo n > b/onlyb/new
diff -ruN a b > fix.patch || echo diff-rc=$?
cp -r a work
cd work
patch -p1 < ../fix.patch || echo rc=$?
cd ..
rm -r a
rm fix.patch

cases.purpose: G55: a one-line diff -c patch applies, forward and with -R; the patch is checked byte for byte first.
cases.script:
printf '1\n' > a
printf '2\n' > b
diff -c --label a --label b a b > p1 || echo diff-rc=$?
cat p1
cp a t
patch t < p1 || echo rc=$?
cat t
patch -R t < p1 || echo rc=$?
cat t
patch -s -c t p1 || echo rc=$?
cat t
rm p1

cases.purpose: G55: diff -c with changes, a deletion, an insertion and an added empty last line, at -C3 and -C1, round trips both ways. (GNU patch itself rejects the -C0 form of a pure deletion as mangled; bash-os applies it.)
cases.script:
seq 20 > A
sed 's/^3$/X/;s/^15$/Y/;/^8$/d;s/^11$/11\n11b/' A > B
echo >> B
for c in 3 1; do
  diff -C$c --label A --label B A B > p || echo diff-rc=$?
  cp A T
  patch T < p || echo rc=$?
  cmp T B && echo same
  patch -R T < p || echo rc=$?
  cmp T A && echo back
done
rm p T

cases.purpose: G55: a hand-written context patch whose old side is left out (pure insertion) and whose new side is left out (pure deletion), with a function name after the stars, applied at an offset.
G55: diff -rcN | patch -p1 creates a file (old side *** 0 ****), removes one (Epoch-dated new side) and changes one; patching an existing file with a creation patch is refused.
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC
mkdir -p a b
printf '1\n2\n' > a/x
printf '1\nTWO\n' > b/x
echo o > a/old
echo n > b/new
diff -rcN a b > fix.patch || echo diff-rc=$?
cp -r a work
cd work
patch -p1 < ../fix.patch || echo rc=$?
ls
cat x new
patch -p1 -N < ../fix.patch || echo rc=$?
cd ..
rm -r a fix.patch

cases.purpose: G55: context patches that add and remove a missing newline at end of file.
cases.script:
printf 'a\nx' > n1
printf 'a\ny\n' > n2
diff -c --label n1 --label n2 n1 n2 > p || echo diff-rc=$?
cp n1 t
patch t < p || echo rc=$?
od -c t
patch -R t < p || echo rc=$?
od -c t
diff -c --label n2 --label n1 n2 n1 > q || echo diff-rc=$?
cp n2 u
patch u < q || echo rc=$?
od -c u
rm p q

cases.purpose: G55: a context hunk that does not apply is saved to F.rej in GNU's context form with both sides listed in full, and the file is kept as F.orig; an already applied patch is detected as reversed.
G55: a rejected hunk of a normal diff is written in GNU's context form too (/dev/null names, no stars, five dashes).
cases.script:
seq 10 | sed 's/^8$/Q/' > T
printf '3c3
< 3
---
> X
8c8
< 8
---
> Y
9a10
> new
' > pn
patch T < pn || echo rc=$?
cat T T.rej
rm pn

cases.purpose: G55: a context hunk whose lines do not match its ranges is a malformed patch (exit 2).
G55: an Epoch-dated creation patch over an existing file and a deletion patch for a missing file get GNU's questions and default answers, with -N, -f, -t, -R and -R -N.
cases.script:
printf -- '--- old\t2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000\n+++ old\t1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000\n@@ -1 +0,0 @@\n-o\n' > pd
printf -- '--- new\t1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000\n+++ new\t2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000000 +0000\n@@ -0,0 +1 @@\n+n\n' > pn
for o in '' -N -f -t -R '-R -N'; do
  rm -f old new *.rej *.orig
  echo "## pd [$o]"
  patch $o < pd || echo rc=$?
  ls
  echo n > new
  echo "## pn [$o]"
  patch $o < pn || echo rc=$?
  ls
  cat new 2>/dev/null || echo no-new
done
rm -f old new *.rej *.orig
: > new
patch < pn || echo rc=$?
cat new

cases.purpose: G80: diff -e a b | patch -s --ed a gives b, including lone-dot lines (diff's s/.// fix-ups).
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
4
5
6
7
' > a
printf '0
1
.
3
..
new
6
7
8
' > b
diff -e a b > s || true
patch -s --ed a s
[[ $(<a) == "$(<b)" ]]
printf 'applied
'
patch -e a < /dev/null || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -e: runs of commands separated by other lines are separate ed hunks; other lines are skipped; s/^\.\././ is not passed on.
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
printf 'junk
2d

3,4d
w
q
0a
first
.
3s/.//
4a
..x
.
5s/^\.\././
' > s
patch -e a s || echo rc=$?
printf '%s
' "$(<a)"

cases.purpose: -e: a command ed rejects prints ? and ed FAILED (status 2); earlier hunks stay applied.
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
printf '9d\n\n20d\n' > s
patch -e a s || echo rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$(<a)"

cases.purpose: -e: a patch with no ed command is only garbage (status 2); an empty one does nothing.
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
printf 'hello\n3 d\n' > s
patch -e a s || echo rc=$?
: > e
patch -e a e || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -e with -o (each hunk applied to the original and appended), -b and --dry-run.
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
printf '9d\n\n1d\n' > s
patch -s -e -o out a s
patch -s -e --dry-run a s
patch -e -b -z .bak a s
printf '%s\n' "$(<out)" "$(<a)" "$(<a.bak)"

cases.purpose: -e: an indented script is announced and applied; an unfinished last line is reported and dropped.
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
printf '  3d\n  1a\n  x\n  .\n' > s
patch -e a s
printf '1d\n2d' > t
patch -e a t
printf '%s\n' "$(<a)"

cases.purpose: -e refuses a directory or symlink operand (status 1).
cases.script:
seq 10 > a
mkdir d
ln -s a l
printf '2d\n' > s
patch -e d s || echo rc=$?
patch -e l s || echo rc=$?
